title: Bhutan for International Visitors: SDF and Visa
meta_description: Bhutan for international visitors: US$100 SDF a night until 31 Aug 2027, the US$40 online visa, Paro flights or the road from India, and the guide rule.
summary: Most international visitors to Bhutan pay a Sustainable Development Fee of US$100 per person per night, a 50% incentive that runs to 31 August 2027, plus a US$40 visa applied for online. You fly into Paro or cross by road from India at Phuentsholing, and a licensed guide is required. Check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: What you pay before you arrive
paras: Bhutan does not charge a minimum daily package any more. Since the country reopened in September 2022, the model is simple: you pay the Sustainable Development Fee, or SDF, for every night you spend in the country, plus a visa fee, and then you pay separately for the hotels, guide, vehicle and meals you choose. The SDF goes to the government for conservation, health, education and infrastructure.

The standard SDF for visitors who pay in US dollars is US$200 per person per night. On 25 August 2023, the Department of Tourism announced a 50% incentive, bringing it to US$100 a night from 1 September 2023 to 31 August 2027. Children aged 6 to 12 pay half, and children under 6 pay nothing. The visa fee is US$40. Indian nationals follow a separate rupee scheme, and Bangladeshi and Maldivian nationals have their own rules. All of this can change, so check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Applying for the visa online
paras: Visas are applied for online through Bhutan's Department of Immigration, before you travel. You can apply yourself, or your Bhutanese tour operator can file it with your itinerary and hotel bookings, which is what most visitors do. You pay the visa fee and the SDF for all your nights as part of the application. When it is approved, you receive an approval letter by email.

Print the letter and carry it with your passport. Airlines flying to Paro may ask for it at check-in, and immigration officers at Paro airport or Phuentsholing check it on arrival. Your passport should have at least six months of validity and a couple of blank pages. Allow a few working days for approval, and more in October and spring when demand is high. Check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Flying into Paro
paras: Paro is Bhutan's international airport, at about 2,200 m in a narrow valley. Scheduled flights are run by two Bhutanese airlines: the national carrier Drukair and Bhutan Airlines. From India they fly from Delhi and Kolkata, and Drukair runs a small number of weekly flights from Bagdogra on an ATR, about 45 minutes. Other Indian cities are served seasonally, and both airlines also fly from regional hubs. Routes and frequencies change by season, so check current status before you travel.

The final approach into Paro is flown visually between the ridges,. From the airport, Thimphu is about 50 km and a little over an hour by road. Your guide meets you in the arrivals hall; under the current rules even this drive needs a licensed guide.

sections.heading: Coming by road from India
paras: Many travellers combine Bhutan with Darjeeling, Sikkim or the Dooars and enter by road at Phuentsholing. Fly to Bagdogra, or take a train to NJP, then drive about 155–170 km, four to five hours, to Jaigaon on the Indian side of the border. From there you walk through the gate to the Phuentsholing terminal.

You will need a valid Indian visa for the India part of the trip, and if you plan to return to India after Bhutan, make sure your visa allows another entry. Foreign nationals also complete Indian exit formalities at Jaigaon before crossing; your operator will know where the office is that week. The road route saves a flight and lets you see the change from the plains at about 300 m to Thimphu at about 2,320 m in one day. Check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: The guide rule
paras: Every international visitor must be accompanied by a certified, licensed guide. A Department of Tourism notification dated 8 April 2026 restated the Tourism Rules and Regulations 2024: guides are required on all tours beyond the first designated checkpoint, including the drive from Paro airport to Thimphu and visits to monuments. For treks, a licensed trekking guide is mandatory.

In practice, this means you book through a licensed Bhutanese operator, who supplies the guide and a Bhutan-registered vehicle with driver. A guide costs about Nu 2,000–3,000 a day and a car with driver about Nu 4,500–6,500 a day, indicative 2026; the Ngultrum is pegged 1:1 to the Indian rupee. Many guides speak excellent English, and some speak other languages; ask in advance if you need one.

sections.heading: Keeping costs sane
paras: On a six-night trip for two adults, the SDF alone is US$1,200 and visas add US$80. Hotels, guide and vehicle come on top. The SDF is fixed, so the savings are in how you plan the rest. These are the levers we pull for our international guests.
list: Travel before 31 August 2027 while the US$100 SDF incentive applies, if your dates are flexible.
Count nights carefully: the SDF is charged per night, so an early-morning arrival and a late departure give you more days for the same fee.
Choose certified 3-star hotels at about Nu 3,000–5,500 a room night with breakfast; tourists must stay in certified hotels or registered homestays.
Share the guide and vehicle with friends; the daily rate is the same for two or six guests.
Travel in March, early April or November rather than October, when rates are at their highest.
Combine Bhutan with Darjeeling or Sikkim by road through Phuentsholing to avoid a return flight to Paro.

sections.heading: A first trip in six nights
paras: This is the route we suggest for a first visit by air. It keeps drives short, puts the Taktsang hike near the end when you are used to the altitude, and leaves Paro close to the airport for the flight out.
list: Night 1, Thimphu: land at Paro, drive about 50 km to Thimphu, evening walk around Clock Tower Square.
Night 2, Thimphu: Buddha Dordenma, the Memorial Chorten built in 1974 for the Third King, and Tashichho Dzong.
Night 3, Punakha: over Dochula and its 108 chortens to Punakha Dzong, built in 1637–38 by the Zhabdrung.

Night 4, Punakha: the walk across the rice fields to Chimi Lhakhang, and a slower afternoon in the valley at about 1,250 m, where it is noticeably warmer than Thimphu. With two extra nights, add Phobjikha for the black-necked cranes from November to February.
Night 5, Paro: drive back west, Rinpung Dzong and the National Museum.
Night 6, Paro: the Taktsang hike, 4–6 hours round trip, with about 500 m of climbing from the car park.
Day 7: fly out of Paro, or drive about 150 km and 5 hours to Phuentsholing to continue into India.

sections.heading: A realistic budget
paras: For a couple on a six-night trip of Thimphu, Punakha and Paro, with 3-star hotels, a private car and a guide, budget roughly US$1,280 for SDF and visas, plus about Nu 70,000–1,20,000 for hotels, guide, vehicle, meals and entry fees for both of you, indicative 2026. Entry fees alone are significant: Paro Taktsang is Nu 1,000 and most dzongs are Nu 500 per adult.

Move up to boutique or 4-star hotels at Nu 7,000–15,000 a room night, or to premium lodges such as COMO Uma in Paro or Gangtey Lodge in Phobjikha, and the hotel line becomes the largest part of the bill. A group of four or six sharing one vehicle and guide brings the per-person cost down noticeably.

faqs.q: How much is the Bhutan SDF for Americans
faqs.a: US citizens, like most international visitors, pay a Sustainable Development Fee of US$100 per person per night until 31 August 2027. That is a 50% incentive on the standard US$200 rate, announced by the Department of Tourism in August 2023. Children aged 6 to 12 pay half and children under 6 pay nothing. The visa fee is a further US$40. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: When does the US$100 SDF offer end
faqs.a: The 50% incentive runs from 1 September 2023 to 31 August 2027, according to the Department of Tourism announcement of 25 August 2023. After that date, unless the government extends it, the SDF is expected to return to the standard US$200 per person per night. If your dates are flexible, travelling before September 2027 saves US$100 a night per adult. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How do I apply for a Bhutan visa
faqs.a: Apply online through Bhutan's Department of Immigration before you travel, or let your licensed Bhutanese tour operator do it for you. You pay the US$40 visa fee and the SDF for every night as part of the application. Once approved, you receive an approval letter by email; print it and carry it with your passport, which should be valid for at least six months. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can I visit Bhutan without a tour guide
faqs.a: No. International visitors must be accompanied by a certified, licensed guide. The Department of Tourism restated this in a notification of 8 April 2026, covering all tours beyond the first designated checkpoint, including the drive from Paro airport to Thimphu and monument visits. Trekkers need a licensed trekking guide. A guide costs about Nu 2,000–3,000 a day, indicative 2026. Check current status before you travel.

Two airlines fly into Paro: Drukair, the national carrier, and Bhutan Airlines. From India they fly from Delhi and Kolkata, and Drukair runs a few weekly flights from Bagdogra, about 45 minutes. Other Indian cities and regional hubs are served on varying schedules. Seats are limited, so book early for October and spring. Routes and frequencies change by season, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can foreigners enter Bhutan by road from India
faqs.a: Yes. The usual crossing is Jaigaon to Phuentsholing, about 155–170 km and four to five hours by road from Bagdogra or Siliguri. You need your Bhutan visa approval and a valid Indian visa, and foreign nationals complete Indian exit formalities at Jaigaon. If you return to India afterwards, make sure your Indian visa allows another entry. Your guide meets you in Phuentsholing. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is there still a minimum daily tariff in Bhutan
faqs.a: No. The old minimum daily package rate was replaced when Bhutan reopened in September 2022. You now pay the SDF per night, plus the visa fee, and choose and pay for your hotel, guide, vehicle and meals separately or as a package. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Do children pay SDF in Bhutan
faqs.a: Children aged 6 to 12 pay half the SDF, which is US$50 a night while the US$100 incentive runs to 31 August 2027. Children under 6 pay no SDF. A family of two adults and one 10-year-old pays US$250 a night in SDF. Monument entry fees are usually half for children too. Check current status before you travel, as rates have changed before.

faqs.q: How many days do you need in Bhutan
faqs.a: Six or seven nights is enough for Thimphu, Punakha and Paro, including the Paro Taktsang hike and a day at Dochula. Add two or three nights for Phobjikha or Bumthang in central Bhutan. Because the SDF is charged per night, every extra night costs US$100 per adult before hotels and guide, so plan the route first and the length second. Check current status before you travel.
